selected_goal.name: Fixed Isometric Camera and Projection Setup
selected_goal.description: Replace the disposable perspective test camera with a fixed orthographic isometric camera configuration matching the GDD's Diablo-1/Ultima-Online-inspired fixed 2.5D isometric presentation.
selected_goal.implementation_scope: Configure the Main Camera to orthographic projection at the correct isometric angle/orthographic size, and fix its position/rotation so it cannot rotate freely. Verify visually against the existing test room. Single behavior: correct fixed isometric camera setup only; no Tilemap authoring or sprite-sorting configuration included.

dependencies.name: Main Camera GameObject
dependencies.evidence: DoorPrototypeSceneBuilder.BuildCamera() sets a perspective camera at (0,8,-8) rotated (45,0,0); confirmed serialized in DoorPrototype.unity.
dependencies.reasoning: This is the object being corrected by the candidate itself, not a blocking external prerequisite.

dependencies.name: Disposable primitive test Floor/Walls
dependencies.evidence: BuildFloor()/BuildWalls() use CreatePrimitive(Plane/Cube); no Tilemap exists yet.
dependencies.reasoning: Sufficient as a disposable rendering target to visually confirm the camera's isometric framing; not a hard blocker for validating camera projection itself.

selected_goal.resource_acquisition_reasoning: No external art/resource is needed; this is a Unity camera component/transform configuration change only. PixelLab is not relevant.
selected_goal.foundation_reasoning: This candidate is itself the focused correction/replacement of the known-incompatible perspective test camera; once corrected, the camera component directly matches the GDD's required fixed orthographic isometric presentation with no remaining incompatible foundation underneath it.
selected_goal.unlock_reasoning: Camera correctness is a hard prerequisite for later visual/art-authoring validation (Tilemap alignment, sprite sorting), but the GDD explicitly decouples the visible isometric layer from the gameplay/simulation layer, so no required gameplay-code feature (movement, doors, spells, enemies) is mechanically blocked by an imperfect camera today; its unlock is real but scoped to the visual layer rather than gameplay-code systems.
selected_goal.decomposition_reasoning: Single testable behavior (camera projection/fixed framing); no Tilemap, sprite, or gameplay logic included.
selected_goal.risk_and_size: Very small, single-component configuration change; quick to verify visually.
selected_goal.reasoning: Low-risk, self-contained correction of a known-incompatible foundation, but its unlock is concentrated in the visual/art-authoring layer rather than required gameplay-code systems.

selection_reason: With Mana now complete, Fixed Isometric Camera and Door Close-Lock-Break Lifecycle Extension are tied on every top-tier readiness/risk dimension: prerequisites_ready=true, resource_acquisition_readiness=high, prototype_readiness=high, foundation_compatibility=compatible, expected_rework_risk=low, implementation_risk=low, and both are labeled unlock_value=medium. The tiebreaker is what that medium unlock actually connects to. Door's own saved reasoning explicitly flags it as a leaf feature that "nothing else depends on." Camera, by contrast, is named directly in the Isometric Tilemap World Foundation candidate's dependency list as a shared_future_dependency (should_promote_to_candidate=true, promoted_candidate_name="Fixed Isometric Camera and Projection Setup") -- it was carved out specifically because the project's single highest-unlock required candidate (Tilemap Foundation: enemy navigation, remaining four rooms, encounter placement) benefits from a correct camera for alignment and sprite-sorting validation. Camera is also the smallest saved risk_and_size ("very small, single-component configuration change") of any remaining candidate, versus Door's "small, single-file extension." Tradeoff acknowledged: Camera's unlock is scoped to the visual/art-authoring layer, which the GDD explicitly decouples from gameplay/simulation logic, so it does not unblock any required gameplay-code system today the way Door's close/lock/break state conceptually feeds into future Dungeon Encounter Agent door-pressure mechanics. But Door's own metadata concedes it has zero downstream dependents, while Camera is a concrete, near-zero-risk stepping stone toward the largest remaining required milestone. That makes Camera the better next pick despite the tie in raw readiness scores.

alternatives_considered.name: Door Close-Lock-Break Lifecycle Extension

alternatives_considered.name: Mouse-Directed Movement and Cursor Targeting
alternatives_considered.reason_not_selected: High unlock_value (feeds Fireball/Frost Field/Force Wave aiming) but weaker foundation profile than Camera or Door: foundation_compatibility=mixed and expected_rework_risk=medium because it must currently rest on the disposable, known-incompatible perspective test camera as a stand-in.

alternatives_considered.name: Isometric Tilemap World Foundation (First Room)
alternatives_considered.reason_not_selected: Highest unlock_value of all remaining candidates (hard prerequisite for enemy navigation, the other four rooms, and encounter placement), but its own saved metadata shows integration_readiness=low and expected_rework_risk/implementation_risk=medium as the project's first Tilemap authoring attempt -- and it explicitly lists the incompatible camera as a dependency, making Camera the more sequenced choice to tackle first.

alternatives_considered.reason_not_selected: Low implementation_risk and required scope, but integration_readiness=low and expected_rework_risk=medium since its real meaning depends on the multi-room persistent run-state architecture that does not exist yet; today's single-room demonstration is likely to need rework later.
